paths.title: Relational Modeling
paths.description: Translate business entities, relationships, and invariants into normalized tables and constraints.
concept: Tables, keys, nullability, and constraints describe which states the database accepts.
A good model reduces duplicated facts and makes invalid relationships difficult to store.
workflow: Start from entities and invariants before writing queries.
Normalization is a reasoning process, not table splitting without purpose.
Represent one-to-many relationships with foreign keys.
Use junction tables for many-to-many relationships.
question: Model a many-to-many relationship
Students can enroll in many courses and courses can contain many students. What structure is appropriate?
A text column listing course names
A junction table with student and course foreign keys
Duplicate the student table for every course
Store everything in one JSON string
A junction table represents each enrollment and can hold relationship attributes.
checklist: Schema integrity review
Confirm that the schema protects important rules.
Application validation is useful, but database constraints protect every writer.
Every table has a stable primary key.
Foreign keys match relationship rules.
Required values are non-null.
Natural uniqueness is constrained.
Ranges use checks or reference tables.
Delete behavior is explicit.
Sensitive fields have appropriate access controls.

paths.title: Query Performance and Indexing
paths.description: Read execution plans and create indexes that support real access patterns.
concept: Indexes trade write cost for read efficiency
An index stores ordered lookup information so the database can avoid scanning every row for supported predicates and joins.
Indexes consume storage and maintenance work, so their column order must match actual queries.
workflow: Use evidence from the execution plan rather than guessing.
Query tuning starts by confirming the workload, data volume, and returned row count.
Capture the exact query and parameters.
Identify scans, joins, sorts, and misestimates.
Add an index only for a demonstrated pattern.
question: Choose composite index order
Queries filter by tenant_id and then order by created_at. Which index is commonly useful?
created_at only
tenant_id, created_at
An unrelated column
No index can help
Leading with the equality filter and following with the ordering column can support both operations.
checklist: Index review checklist
Confirm that an index improves the workload rather than one example.
Production performance depends on realistic cardinality and concurrent reads and writes.
The query is frequent or important.
Column order matches predicates and ordering.
The plan actually uses the index.
Write overhead is acceptable.
Duplicate indexes are removed.
Statistics are current.
Performance is tested with representative data.

paths.title: Transactions and Recovery
paths.description: Use isolation, locking, backups, and migrations to preserve data through concurrency and failure.
concept: A database is not protected merely because backups exist; restoration must produce a consistent, usable system.
Transactions protect individual changes, while backup and recovery procedures address larger failures.
workflow: Change production data without assuming an instantaneous deployment.
Compatible, reversible stages reduce downtime and rollback risk.
Add new structures in a backward-compatible form.
Deploy code that can use old and new shapes.
question: Avoid a long blocking migration
Which approach is safest for adding a required column to a very large active table?
Add it with an expensive rewrite and no plan
Stage a nullable column, backfill, validate, then enforce the constraint
Delete the table first
Disable backups
A staged expand-and-contract migration limits locks and keeps versions compatible.
checklist: Database recovery readiness
Verify that data can be restored after corruption or loss.
Recovery objectives should be defined in business terms and tested regularly.
Recovery point and time objectives are defined.
Backups are encrypted and monitored.
Restore procedures are documented.
Restores are tested on a schedule.
Migration rollback is understood.
Replication lag and failover are observable.
Consistency is verified after recovery.
